bull_bear.body:
- Project execution and delay risk — As a project-based EPC/infrastructure business, execution delays can affect profitability and cash flows; managed through detailed planning, milestone monitoring, site reviews, client coordination and escalation of critical constraints.
- Cost overrun / margin risk — Estimated cost-to-complete can move against the Company, requiring selective bidding, budget controls, procurement planning, price benchmarking and continuous review of cost estimates.
- Working-capital and collection risk — The infrastructure business requires funding of mobilisation, procurement, execution and receivables before billing converts to cash; billing discipline, certification tracking, debtor reviews and banking arrangements are used to manage this.
- Customer/sector concentration risk — Managed through diversification across sectors, geographies and customer categories, with evaluation of payment track record and contract terms.
- Regulatory, safety and environmental risk — Compliance monitoring, site-level safety protocols, statutory approvals, training and engagement of technical professionals are used to manage this risk.
- Equipment and mining-operation risk — Reliance on HEMM fleets and mining/transportation equipment exposes the Company to operational risk, managed via preventive maintenance, utilisation monitoring, insurance and deployment of experienced personnel.
- Human-resource risk — Growth depends on the ability to attract, develop and retain engineers, project managers and skilled site teams; managed through recruitment, training, succession planning and retention measures.
- Leverage and debt-servicing risk — Higher utilisation of working-capital facilities and borrowings to support expanded business scale increased debt-equity ratios and finance costs; debt service coverage remained comfortable but lower than the previous year.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.body:
- Selective participation in projects offering appropriate risk-adjusted returns and payment visibility.
- Expansion in water infrastructure and mining, supported by the Company's growing execution capabilities.
- Strengthening of project planning, procurement, billing, collection and working-capital controls.
- Development of a diversified Group platform through subsidiaries, joint ventures and strategic investments.

outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body: During FY2025-26 the Company undertook a strategic transformation from a primarily EPC-focused enterprise into a diversified infrastructure group, expanding into Water Infrastructure and Mining Development Operations. It established a wholly owned subsidiary, GRV Global L.L.C-FZ, in Dubai, UAE (incorporated 12.04.2025) to expand operations internationally, intending to subscribe to 100% of its share capital; the entity is yet to commence operations. It also acquired an initial 39.78% equity stake in Kandoi Transport Limited (associated/acquired 13.03.2026), which was increased to 60% in the current financial year, to support business growth and create operational synergies in transportation, building an integrated mining services value chain. The Group structure also expanded through the Trivanta Resources Private Limited subsidiary and the Ganesh Netsoft JV Networks joint venture.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's sustained infrastructure investment cycle, water security focus, expansion in mining and logistics, industrial development and urban infrastructure provide a favourable medium-term backdrop for the Group.
- Public investment (Union Budget FY2025-26 capex, PM Gati Shakti, National Infrastructure Pipeline, railway modernisation, highways, water supply, urban infrastructure, energy transition) is expected to sustain a healthy opportunity pipeline for organised EPC and infrastructure service providers.
- Water security is a national priority, with continued investment under the Jal Jeevan Mission, urban water supply programmes, sewerage networks, treatment plants and reuse infrastructure creating opportunities across design, construction, electromechanical works and O&M.
- The mining sector is gaining strategic importance given India's infrastructure and manufacturing requirements, with greater emphasis on domestic resource availability, commercial mining, mechanisation and production efficiency creating opportunities for organised contractors.
- Mining contracts can provide long-tenure revenue visibility but require strong equipment planning, operating controls, safety systems and cost monitoring.
- Execution will remain dependent on timely clearances, land availability, customer funding, commodity-price stability and disciplined working-capital management.
- The Company closed the year with a healthy order book of approximately ₹2,283.70 crore, providing medium-term execution visibility, spanning mining, water infrastructure, civic utilities, educational infrastructure, telecom and railway-related works and other EPC activities.
- The consolidated order book has expanded to over ₹4,315 crore, providing revenue visibility over the coming period per the Chairman's message.
